summary:
**BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:** SoftBank Group signs for power and data-centre equipment through one subsidiary, SB Energy. SB Energy is building OpenAI's Milam County campus in Texas (about 753 MW-IT), has leased its planned 8.0 GW-IT PORTS-Pike campus in Ohio to OpenAI, and is in IPO registration; its S-1 says the roughly 9.2 GW of gas generation planned beside PORTS is being developed by a different SoftBank affiliate. Since 30 September 2026 SoftBank has also owned DigitalBridge, which manages, but does not own, the funds that control Vantage, Switch, DataBank and other platforms. Everything else is capital: about 13% of OpenAI (USD 64.6bn invested), 86.7% of Arm, and all of Ampere and Graphcore. For a vendor, SoftBank is a door at SB Energy and a directory at DigitalBridge.

**BACKGROUND.** Per company filings, the registrant is SoftBank Group Corp. (TSE: 9984, Prime Market), a Tokyo pure holding company whose fiscal year ends 31 March; Masayoshi Son holds 32.73% of the shares. FY2025 (to 31 March 2026) net income attributable to owners was ¥5,002.3bn on net sales of ¥7,798.7bn, driven by a ¥6,730.4bn investment gain on OpenAI. Net asset value rose from ¥25.7tn to ¥40.1tn over the year and stood at ¥72.3tn on 30 June 2026, with loan-to-value at 13.0%. SoftBank reports four segments: the investment business of the holding companies, the SoftBank Vision Funds, SoftBank (the listed telco SoftBank Corp., 40.1% held and consolidated) and AI Computing (Arm, Ampere and Graphcore). DigitalBridge's 8-K records the merger completed on 30 September 2026 at USD 16.00 a share in cash, with the acquiring parent wholly owned by SoftBank Group Overseas GK. SoftBank states the price as about USD 3.1bn for all the common stock, against a total enterprise value of about USD 4.0bn at announcement, and DigitalBridge continues as a 'separately managed platform, led by Marc Ganzi'. The USD 5.375bn purchase of ABB's robotics business is signed, not closed.
ecosystemRole: We assess SoftBank Group as three different counterparties under one name. Through SB Energy it is a buyer: SB Energy's S-1 says it buys solar modules, battery components, high-voltage transformers, switchgear and inverters itself, lets construction to EPC contractors (Turner, DPR, Kiewit, SOLV Energy and others), and has not yet chosen the backup-generation engines for PORTS. Through DigitalBridge it is a manager: it owns the general partner of funds whose capital is almost entirely third-party, so Vantage, Switch and DataBank sign their own orders under fund governance. Through Stargate, OpenAI and the Portsmouth Consortium it is a convenor and financier that buys nothing. A seller works SB Energy directly and uses DigitalBridge to find the platforms.

productsAndServices.name: SB Energy (Energy Global, LP) — AI data-centre campuses and power
productsAndServices.description: SoftBank's US developer of solar, battery storage and AI data-centre campuses, founded with SoftBank backing in 2019. The legal entity SoftBank reports is Energy Global, LP, which its Securities Report shows 100% held at 31 March 2026. SoftBank and its affiliates have contributed about USD 3.2bn of cash. The listing vehicle, SB Energy, Inc. (a Texas corporation), filed an S-1 on 1 September 2026 and an amended S-1 on 21 September; no price range or ownership percentages have been filed. After the IPO SoftBank expects to hold more than 50% of the vote, making SB Energy a 'controlled company'. Its campuses are Cosmos (Austin, about 50 MW-IT, leased to a SoftBank affiliate), Milam County (about 753 MW-IT, leased to OpenAI) and PORTS-Pike in Ohio (about 8.0 GW-IT, leased to OpenAI on 17 August 2026). It had about 2.2 GW of solar and storage operating at 30 June 2026.
highlights: The S-1 says SB Energy procures directly 'solar modules, battery energy storage system components, high-voltage transformers, switchgear, inverters', and procures long-lead equipment 'early, at portfolio scale and across multiple suppliers'
Construction is let to EPC contractors — 'Turner, DPR, Kiewit and SOLV Energy' for data centres; SOLV, Blattner, Dashiell, CSI Electrical and Rosendin for power
Backlog of about USD 439bn (about USD 430bn data centres, USD 10bn power) and about USD 178bn of capex tied to signed contracts, about USD 48bn of it within 24 months (S-1/A2)
PORTS gas: 'being developed by an affiliate of SoftBank that is not our subsidiary' (S-1/A2); SoftBank is secretariat of the 21-member Portsmouth Consortium
Investors besides SoftBank: OpenAI (USD 500m preferred equity, January 2026, plus warrants), NVIDIA (USD 3.0bn of Class N stock and prepaid forward at the IPO)
productsAndServices.positioning: Within the group, the only operating business that signs for generation, batteries, high-voltage gear and data-centre construction. SB Energy names Digital Realty, Equinix, QTS, Vantage, Switch, CyrusOne and Aligned as data-centre competitors, and Clearway, NextEra and AES in power. Its distinguishing feature is that it is tenanted by its own investors: SoftBank at Cosmos and OpenAI at Milam and PORTS.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Long-term triple-net data-centre leases (15–20 years) and fixed-price power purchase agreements (10–25 years); project finance, tax equity and, from the IPO, public equity
targetSegments: AI labs and hyperscalers (OpenAI, SoftBank affiliates)
Utilities and load-serving entities buying solar and storage
productsAndServices.roadmap: Initial public offering on Nasdaq and Nasdaq Texas (ticker SBE) — unpriced at 4 October 2026, with the delay reported as a valuation gap; PORTS first phase targeted for 2028, buildings 1–9 by 2031 and 10–17 by 2032; Milam buildings in 2027–2028

productsAndServices.name: DigitalBridge — digital-infrastructure investment manager
productsAndServices.description: Acquired on 30 September 2026. DigitalBridge describes itself as 'a leading global investment manager in digital infrastructure' with USD 40.2bn of fee-earning equity under management at 30 June 2026. That total splits into USD 17.3bn in the DigitalBridge Partners fund series, USD 15.3bn in co-investment vehicles, USD 3.3bn at InfraBridge, USD 3.3bn in core, credit and liquid strategies, and USD 1.0bn in separately capitalised portfolio companies. SoftBank's announcement put total assets managed at USD 108bn. DigitalBridge does not consolidate its funds, and its general-partner commitment is small. In the 10-Q's words: 'minimum capital commitments to our sponsored funds ranging from 0.03% to 0.72%', plus 1.43%–4.29% as a general-partner affiliate in the flagship funds. Its own balance sheet holds 'minority equity stakes in DataBank and Vantage NA SDC'.
highlights: Portfolio companies SoftBank listed as examples: Vantage, Switch and DataBank (data centres); GD Towers, Vertical Bridge, JTOWER (towers); Zayo, Netomnia, WOW! (fibre); AtlasEdge, Boingo, FreshWave (edge)
Yondr: 'La Caisse … has assumed joint control' alongside DigitalBridge-managed vehicles (closed 1 July 2025)
Signed, not closed: ArcLight Capital Partners for up to USD 1.05bn (USD 650m base plus up to USD 400m contingent), conditional on the SoftBank merger

InfraBridge, DigitalBridge's infrastructure-fund arm, is Invenergy's equity partner in its North American natural gas portfolio, per Invenergy: 'we entered into equity partnership with InfraBridge in 2018'
Takanock, backed by DigitalBridge and ArcLight with USD 500m, plans on-site gas generation for data centres (reported)
productsAndServices.positioning: SoftBank calls DigitalBridge a 'separately managed platform, led by Marc Ganzi'. The purchase was a manager with fee contracts, carried interest and small general-partner stakes. The platforms' equity belongs to third-party investors such as Silver Lake, PSP, GIC, ADIA, AustralianSuper and MEAG at Vantage, and IFM and Aware Super at Switch.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Closed-end flagship funds (DBP I–III; DBP III closed at USD 7.2bn in October 2025), co-investment vehicles, InfraBridge and core funds sold to institutional limited partners
targetSegments: Data-centre, tower, fibre and edge platforms
productsAndServices.roadmap: ArcLight closing: conditional on the SoftBank merger, which closed 30 September 2026; the outside date is the later of 31 March 2027 and six months after the SoftBank closing

productsAndServices.name: OpenAI stake and the Stargate programme
productsAndServices.description: SoftBank's largest single asset. SoftBank Vision Fund 2 has invested USD 64.6bn in OpenAI since September 2024; SoftBank puts its ownership at about 13% after the third USD 10bn tranche of the 2026 round, executed 1 October 2026. Its cumulative investment stood at USD 34.6bn on 31 March 2026, before the 2026 round began; the 2025 round had taken the stake to about 11% on 26 December 2025. SoftBank calls itself 'a minority shareholder of OpenAI' with 'only a limited ability to influence' it. Stargate was announced on 22 January 2025 as 'a new company which intends to invest $500 billion over the next four years'. Its 'initial equity funders' were SoftBank, OpenAI, Oracle and MGX, 'with SoftBank having financial responsibility and OpenAI having operational responsibility', and Masayoshi Son as chairman. No SoftBank document states its own dollar commitment or percentage in the Stargate entity.
highlights: The September 2025 expansion named two SoftBank-partnered sites: Lordstown, Ohio, where 'SoftBank has broken ground', and Milam County, Texas, 'in partnership with SB Energy'
In practice SoftBank's Stargate sites are delivered by SB Energy as developer, owner and operator. Lordstown is absent from the 'three core locations' SoftBank listed in August 2026
The Information reported in February 2026 that the Stargate joint venture 'hasn't hired any staff' and had become bilateral (reported; all three companies declined to comment)
SB OAI Japan: a 50:50 venture between OpenAI and C Holdings (SoftBank Corp. 51%, SoftBank Group 49%) selling 'Crystal intelligence' in Japan
Stargate UAE (May 2025): a 1 GW cluster 'built by G42 and operated by OpenAI and Oracle', with SoftBank among the partners
productsAndServices.positioning: SoftBank is the largest outside financier in OpenAI's 2025 and 2026 rounds. S&P moved SoftBank's outlook to negative on 3 March 2026, saying the follow-on investment means 'it will take longer than we had assumed for the company to restore the liquidity and quality of its investment assets'.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Preferred shares held in SoftBank Vision Fund 2 that convert on an OpenAI listing; financed with a USD 40bn bridge (repaid and cancelled by 30 September 2026), a USD 10bn loan secured on the OpenAI shares and about USD 11.1bn of senior notes
targetSegments: OpenAI-leased AI campuses through SB Energy
productsAndServices.roadmap: OpenAI's 2026 round fully funded on 1 October 2026; fair value is marked quarterly through profit and loss

productsAndServices.name: AI Computing — Arm, Ampere and Graphcore
productsAndServices.description: A segment created in the October–December 2025 quarter by combining Arm, Ampere and Graphcore. SoftBank's Securities Report shows Arm Holdings plc at 86.7% (voting), and Arm's own 20-F gives 86.4% at 21 May 2026, with 72.0% of Arm's shares pledged under a SoftBank margin loan. SoftBank completed its USD 6.5bn purchase of Ampere Computing on 25 November 2025, buying from Carlyle, Oracle and Arm. Graphcore is wholly owned and is the first tenant at SB Energy's Cosmos campus in Austin. In Q1 FY2026 the segment's net sales were ¥175.3bn and its segment loss ¥200.8bn, driven by R&D.
highlights: Arm launched its first own silicon, the 'Arm AGI CPU', in March 2026 (SoftBank Group Report 2026)
Rene Haas, Arm's CEO, also became CEO of SoftBank Group International on 21 April 2026
Arm's 20-F says Arm is engaged to advise on or design chips for affiliates of SoftBank Group
productsAndServices.positioning: Chip designers that supply processors to the AI build-out rather than buyers of power equipment. Arm sits in NVIDIA's Grace CPUs, and Ampere sells Arm-based server CPUs.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Licensing and royalties (Arm); server processors (Ampere); AI accelerators (Graphcore)

productsAndServices.name: SoftBank Vision Funds (SVF1, SVF2, Latin America)
productsAndServices.description: SoftBank Investment Advisers manages SVF1, and SB Global Advisers manages SVF2 and the Latin America fund; both managers are wholly owned. Third-party investors committed most of SVF1's capital, and SoftBank holds a 33.6% share. SVF2 is effectively SoftBank's own money: SoftBank committed USD 140.6bn of its USD 143.2bn, with management co-investment making up the rest, and SVF2 holds the OpenAI stake. Vision Fund gains were ¥6,638.6bn in FY2025, ¥6,465.5bn of which came from OpenAI, against ¥387.6bn in FY2024.
highlights: SoftBank sold all its NVIDIA shares in October 2025 (32.1m shares, USD 5.83bn) and most of its T-Mobile stake (75.4m shares, USD 16.25bn) to fund OpenAI
Equity value of holdings at 30 June 2026: SVF2 ¥19.29tn, SVF1 ¥3.60tn, Latin America ¥1.00tn (data sheet)
productsAndServices.positioning: A late-stage growth investor. Its AI-infrastructure relevance now runs almost entirely through SVF2's OpenAI position.

productsAndServices.name: SoftBank segment — SoftBank Corp., LY Corporation, PayPay; SB Neo
productsAndServices.description: SoftBank Corp. (TSE: 9434) is the Japanese telco. SoftBank Group holds 40.1% and consolidates it because it controls the company in practice. LY Corporation (62.4%, indirect) and PayPay (90.6%, listed on Nasdaq as PAYP since March 2026) sit in the same segment. The segment's Q1 FY2026 net sales were ¥1,813.9bn and its segment income ¥292.5bn. SB Neo, Inc., announced on 2 July 2026, is a US neocloud owned 51% by SoftBank Corp. and 49% by SoftBank Group. It plans to start services in FY2027 'leveraging the SoftBank Group's 10-gigawatt-scale energy and AI infrastructure currently under development'.
highlights: SB Neo plans to finance compute through project companies with non-recourse loans and sell to hyperscalers
SoftBank Corp. plans 'gigawatt-scale AI data centers in Japan' (SB Neo release)
productsAndServices.positioning: The group's operating cash engine. SoftBank Corp. is a separate listed actor with its own Japanese data-centre plans, recorded in this dossier as a consolidated subsidiary rather than given its own slug.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Telecom, internet and payments services in Japan
productsAndServices.roadmap: SB Neo services from the fiscal year ending March 2028

productsAndServices.name: France AI data-centre programme
productsAndServices.description: On 30 May 2026 SoftBank committed 'to develop and operate 5 GW of AI data center capacity in France, representing an investment of up to €75 billion'. The first phase is €45bn for 3.1 GW in Hauts-de-France by 2031, at Dunkirk (Loon-Plage), Bosquel and Bouchain. SoftBank 'will work with SB Energy and other strategic partners'. At Bosquel, a joint venture majority-owned by SoftBank and formed with Sesterce was selected to develop and operate a 1 GW campus. At the Port of Dunkirk there will be two facilities: one operated by SoftBank to manufacture enclosures, and one operated by Schneider Electric to integrate data-centre power modules.
highlights: EDF is named on the Bouchain site
A commitment and a plan, not a completed project
productsAndServices.positioning: The only place SoftBank itself, rather than SB Energy, is the stated developer and operator of data-centre capacity.

productsAndServices.name: Holding-company investments and pending acquisitions
productsAndServices.description: Direct stakes held by the holding company, notably Intel common stock (USD 2bn at USD 23 a share, executed September 2025; ¥1,332.9bn gain in Q1 FY2026), the remaining T-Mobile shares and SB Northstar. SoftBank agreed on 8 October 2025 to buy ABB's robotics business for USD 5.375bn. SoftBank lists it as 'Planned in 2026', has arranged USD 1.75bn of non-recourse acquisition finance, and has announced no completion. SoftBank names four areas of focus: 'AI chips, AI robots, AI data centers, and energy'.
highlights: ABB Robotics: about 7,000 employees, headquartered in Zürich; approvals needed in the EU, China and the US
productsAndServices.roadmap: ABB Robotics closing expected in the second half of 2026 (SoftBank and ABB)

strategyRead: **(High confidence)** We assess that **SoftBank is a door at SB Energy and a directory everywhere else**. SB Energy's S-1 says it procures 'solar modules, battery energy storage system components, high-voltage transformers, switchgear, inverters' itself and lets turnkey construction to named EPC contractors. No other SoftBank business states any such purchasing. DigitalBridge, the Vision Funds and the OpenAI stake hold equity; Arm, Ampere and Graphcore design chips. Basis: the S-1/A2 procurement and execution-model sections, SoftBank's segment table and DigitalBridge's 10-Q. A power-equipment seller qualifies at SB Energy's supply-chain team and its EPCs, not at SoftBank Group.

**(High confidence)** We assess that **SoftBank bought DigitalBridge's management rights, not its platforms**. DigitalBridge consolidates none of its funds and calls itself 'an agent of the fund'. Its general-partner commitment runs from 0.03% to 0.72%, plus 1.43%–4.29% as a general-partner affiliate. Its own balance sheet holds only 'minority equity stakes in DataBank and Vantage NA SDC'. The fund investors' consent was a closing condition. Basis: DigitalBridge's Q2 2026 10-Q, its merger proxy and the closing 8-K. SoftBank therefore reaches Vantage and Switch the way BlackRock reaches Aligned through GIP: by appointing the manager, under duties owed to outside investors (the duties are our inference from the managers' SEC registration, not a filed statement).

**(Moderate confidence)** We assess that **SoftBank's Stargate role has turned into a landlord relationship run through SB Energy**. SoftBank was named an initial equity funder with 'financial responsibility' in January 2025, but no SoftBank document states its commitment to the Stargate entity. Its delivered sites — Milam County and PORTS-Pike — are owned by SB Energy and leased to OpenAI. The Information reported in February 2026 that the joint venture had hired no staff. SB Energy's S-1 never uses the word 'Stargate'. Basis: SoftBank's releases of January and September 2025, its August 2026 deck and the S-1. The judgment is moderate because the Stargate entity's current form is undisclosed.

**(Moderate confidence)** We assess that **the ~9.2 GW of gas generation at PORTS is the largest unassigned procurement in the SoftBank orbit, and its owner of record is not yet settled**. The S-1 says the plants are 'being developed by an affiliate of SoftBank that is not our subsidiary', funded through 'an investment vehicle jointly owned by the U.S. Department of Commerce and an entity established by the Japan Bank for International Cooperation'. The DOE fact sheet says 'SB Energy will build new gas-fired generation', and SB Energy's PORTS microsite says the plants 'will be owned by the U.S. Government'. An SB Energy spokesperson told Inside Climate News that SoftBank 'has reserved sufficient gas turbines from multiple sources including GE Vernova' (reported). The Portsmouth Consortium names the suppliers who intend to take part, not the ones under contract.

**(Moderate confidence)** We assess that **OpenAI concentration, not appetite, limits how much SoftBank itself can commit to equipment**. OpenAI is SoftBank's largest asset (USD 64.6bn invested), is pledged against a USD 10bn loan, and pushed S&P's outlook to negative. The CFO says new AI infrastructure will use project finance 'that does not impact our LTV', with SoftBank's risk 'capped at its equity contribution', and that DigitalBridge's investee debt will not 'directly impact SBG's credit profile'. Basis: SoftBank Group Report 2026 and the rating actions. Expect project-level, non-recourse buyers (SB Energy's project companies, SB Neo's special-purpose companies), not SoftBank Group, on the purchase orders.

**(Low confidence)** We assess that **DigitalBridge may become SoftBank's channel into on-site power**. The ArcLight acquisition (signed, conditional on the SoftBank merger) would add a generation investor with a development pipeline above 15 GW. Takanock, backed by DigitalBridge and ArcLight, plans 400 MW of on-site gas at a Virginia campus (reported). The merger proxy records Son and Ganzi discussing 'power bank energy capacity for data centers'. Weak because ArcLight has not closed and no SoftBank document assigns DigitalBridge a power role.

**Collection gaps:** SoftBank's dollar commitment to, and share of, the Stargate entity; the name and ownership of the SoftBank affiliate developing PORTS gas and who holds the turbine reservations; SoftBank's economic share of SB Energy after the OpenAI, Ares and NVIDIA instruments (the S-1's percentages are blank); the current SoftBank titles of Ippei Mimura and Varun Aravapally, two of DigitalBridge's new directors; whether Lordstown remains a data-centre site; the USD amount of the Arm margin loan (reports conflict); a full-year consensus for FY2025 (none located in a loadable source).

**INDICATORS TO WATCH** — *SB Energy IPO pricing (reported delayed to mid-to-late October):* a 424B4 would give the first public value for the platform and SoftBank's stake. *AEP Ohio definitive agreements (AEP expected them in Q3 2026; its Q3 call is due in late October):* execution and the OPSB hearing on the Baku–Gavin 765 kV line (27 October) gate PORTS beyond its first 0.8 GW. *Q2 FY2026 results, 10 November 2026:* the first quarter consolidating DigitalBridge and the first with a full OpenAI position at about 13%. *ArcLight closing:* confirms Judgment 6. *Any turbine order or engineering award naming the PORTS gas developer:* settles Judgment 4. *ABB Robotics closing:* expected in the second half of 2026.

It then committed USD 30.0bn in 2026 at a USD 730bn pre-money valuation, paid in three USD 10bn tranches, the last on 1 October 2026. SoftBank describes itself as 'a minority shareholder of OpenAI' with 'only a limited ability to influence' it. Separately, OpenAI is SB Energy's tenant at Milam County and PORTS-Pike, OpenAI and SoftBank each put USD 500m into SB Energy in January 2026, and the two run SB OAI Japan as a 50:50 venture.

relationships.via: DigitalBridge (manager of the funds that lead Vantage's ownership)
relationships.note: A DigitalBridge portfolio company: since 30 September 2026 SoftBank owns the manager whose funds lead Vantage's ownership.
relationships.context: SoftBank's Q3 FY2025 deck lists Vantage first among DigitalBridge's 'Key Portfolio Companies', describing it as 'building and operating hyperscale campus data centers globally'. The equity belongs to DigitalBridge-managed funds and co-investors, including Silver Lake, PSP, GIC, ADIA, AustralianSuper and MEAG. DigitalBridge's own balance sheet holds only a minority equity-method stake in Vantage NA SDC, the stabilised North American portfolio. SoftBank's reach into Vantage's equipment decisions runs through DigitalBridge's board and fund governance, not through ownership. DigitalBridge's merger proxy records that Vantage's October 2025 Stargate site partnership with OpenAI and Oracle came before the deal.

relationships.via: DigitalBridge (manager of the funds that co-own Switch with IFM)
relationships.note: A DigitalBridge portfolio company: SoftBank now owns the manager of the funds that took Switch private with IFM Investors in 2022.
relationships.context: SoftBank's Q3 FY2025 deck lists Switch among DigitalBridge's 'Key Portfolio Companies', as 'focused on developing AI-ready, large-scale campus data centers across the U.S.'. DigitalBridge's 10-K and 10-Q do not name Switch; it is held in DigitalBridge-managed funds alongside IFM Investors and Aware Super, and DigitalBridge does not consolidate it. SoftBank's link is the manager, not the equity.

relationships.note: Fellow initial equity funder of Stargate and partner in its September 2025 site expansion; also the seller of its Ampere stake to SoftBank.
relationships.context: The 22 January 2025 announcement names 'SoftBank, OpenAI, Oracle, and MGX' as Stargate's initial equity funders. The September 2025 release added five sites, three led with Oracle and two partnered by SoftBank (Lordstown, Ohio and Milam County, Texas). Separately, Oracle's Project Denver Holdings held 32.27% of Ampere Computing and sold it to SoftBank in the USD 6.5bn acquisition completed on 25 November 2025.

relationships.note: Fellow initial equity funder of Stargate, named with SoftBank, OpenAI and Oracle in the January 2025 announcement.
relationships.context: SoftBank's 22 January 2025 release names MGX among the four initial equity funders, with SoftBank holding 'financial responsibility'. Neither SoftBank nor MGX discloses its commitment. SoftBank's September 2025 expansion release does not name MGX.

relationships.via: Stargate technology partner; exclusive compute provider at SB Energy's PORTS-Pike campus
relationships.note: A Stargate technology partner, and since August 2026 the exclusive compute provider and lead credit support at SoftBank's PORTS-Pike campus; SoftBank sold its NVIDIA shares in October 2025.
relationships.context: The January 2025 Stargate announcement names NVIDIA among the technology partners. On 17 August 2026 NVIDIA agreed to host its compute exclusively at SB Energy's PORTS-Pike campus, to give residual value guaranties on the first 4.25 GW-IT, and to invest USD 1.5bn in SB Energy (USD 3.0bn in total with a prepaid forward). SoftBank had sold its whole NVIDIA holding, 32.1m shares for USD 5.83bn, in October 2025 to fund OpenAI.

relationships.note: Partner in Stargate UAE, the 1 GW Abu Dhabi cluster G42 builds and OpenAI and Oracle operate.
relationships.context: SoftBank's 22 May 2025 release says Stargate UAE 'will be built by G42 and operated by OpenAI and Oracle', and that the collaboration 'will also include Cisco … and SoftBank Group'. SoftBank's specific role is not stated.

relationships.note: Agreed buyer of ABB's robotics business for USD 5.375bn; signed on 8 October 2025 and not completed as of 1 October 2026.
relationships.context: SoftBank's 8 October 2025 release states a total purchase price of USD 5.375bn and expected closing in mid-to-late 2026, subject to EU, Chinese and US approvals. Its August 2026 investor deck lists the deal as 'Planned in 2026' and notes USD 1.75bn of non-recourse acquisition financing. No completion has been announced.

relationships.note: Partner in SoftBank's French data-centre programme: Schneider Electric is to operate a facility at the Port of Dunkirk integrating data-centre power modules.
relationships.context: SoftBank's 30 May 2026 announcement of up to 5 GW in France describes two facilities at Dunkirk: one operated by SoftBank to manufacture enclosures, and one operated by Schneider Electric to integrate data-centre power modules. It is an announced plan, with no order or volume stated.

policyExposure.exposure: On 23 December 2019 SoftBank and certain of its subsidiaries entered into a National Security Agreement with CFIUS over SoftBank's ownership of SB Energy's US operations, supplemented on 20 September 2021. SB Energy's S-1 says the agreement imposes 'restrictions on vendors, cybersecurity requirements and project sale notification procedures', including approval or non-objection for certain vendor relationships, and that these restrictions 'have delayed, and may continue to delay, our ability to onboard vendors'.
policyExposure.mitigation: SB Energy says it maintains 'approved vendor lists for SCADA, networking and other critical operational technology systems'.

policyExposure.regime: U.S.–Japan Strategic Trade and Investment Agreement
policyExposure.exposure: The roughly 9.2 GW Portsmouth Powered Land Project beside SB Energy's PORTS-Pike campus was named in the first tranche of projects under the USD 550bn US–Japan investment framework. The DOE puts Japanese funding at USD 33.3bn. SB Energy's S-1 expects the plants to be funded 'through an investment vehicle jointly owned by the U.S. Department of Commerce and an entity established by the Japan Bank for International Cooperation' and developed by a SoftBank affiliate that is not SB Energy's subsidiary. It warns that the funding 'may be delayed, reduced or withdrawn'. SoftBank Group is secretariat of the 21-member Portsmouth Consortium formed around the project.
